sections.body:
The weather is what the sky and the air are doing right now. The sun is out. The clouds are grey. The rain is falling. The wind is strong.

Weather is not the same as climate. Weather is today. Climate is the whole season, or the whole year. *It is raining today* is weather. *It rains a lot in this season* is climate.

Why do people talk about the weather so much? Because it changes what everybody does. It decides what you wear, whether you can play outside, and what you eat for lunch. In Vietnam, a child in the south sees a bright sky in February, while a child in the north sees snow. Same planet, different days.

The weather is also the easiest subject to talk about with anyone. You do not need to know the person. You do not need a good reason. You can always talk about the sky.

In this article you will learn the words for the sky, how to start a weather talk, and how to dress for the day ahead.
examples: What is the weather like today?
sections.heading: What the weather is

sections.body:
A weather talk has a shape. It goes: hello, the weather, and then the day.

Say hello first. A weather question on its own can sound cold. *Hello Mai. How is it going?* comes first.

Say what you see. *It is very sunny today.* *It is raining a little.* You do not need to check your phone. Look up.

Say how it feels. *It is so hot today.* *It is a bit chilly this morning.* This is the part people really want to hear.

Then say what you are doing. *I am wearing a hat because of the sun.* *I am wearing my boots because of the rain.* Now it is a real conversation.

Or ask one question back. *How is it where you are?* *Are you going to play outside today?* Now it is a two-way talk.

That is all a weather talk needs. It takes about thirty seconds, and it makes people glad to see you.
examples: Hello Mai. How is it going?
It is so hot today, I am sweating.
How is the weather where you are?
sections.heading: How to start a weather talk

sections.body:
These are the words for the sky. Learn them and you can describe any day.

Sunny means the sun is shining and there are few clouds. *It is a sunny day* is a happy sentence.

Cloudy means the sky has clouds in it. A cloudy day can still be warm or cold. Clouds are just a sky, not a temperature.

Rainy means water is falling from the clouds. In Vietnamese we call it *mưa*, and there are many kinds of rain: small, heavy, and the kind that waits for the afternoon.

Windy means the air is moving fast. Windy is not a temperature either. A windy day can be hot or freezing.

Cold means the temperature is low. *Cold* and *cool* are different: cool is a little low, cold is much lower.

Hot means the temperature is high. Hot and warm are different too: warm is pleasant, hot makes you thirsty.

And **weather** is the word for all of it together. You say *the weather*, never *a weather*.
sections.heading: The weather words, one by one

terms.example: It is sunny, so we can play outside.
terms.gloss: The sun is shining and there are few clouds. A sunny day is a happy day.

terms.example: It is cloudy this morning, but it is still warm.
terms.gloss: The sky has clouds in it. Clouds are about the sky, not about the temperature.

terms.example: It is rainy, so take an umbrella.
terms.gloss: Water is falling from the clouds. There is light rain and heavy rain.

terms.example: It is windy, so my hat keeps blowing away.
terms.gloss: The air is moving fast. A windy day can be hot or freezing.

terms.example: It is cold outside, so I am wearing my coat.
terms.gloss: The temperature is low. Cold is lower than cool.

sections.body:
Somebody asks you about the weather. Here is a good answer.

First, look up. You cannot see the weather from inside your head.

Then, look at the sky. Sun, clouds, rain, or clear blue.

Next, check how it feels. Put your hand out. Warm air, cool air, or cold air.

After that, add the detail. Is the wind strong? Is the rain heavy? Is the sun hot enough to make you squint?

Then say what you are wearing or doing, because that is what the person really wanted to know. *I have a raincoat on, it started five minutes ago.*

And if you do not know, that is fine too. *I have not been outside yet today.* An honest answer is better than a guess.
examples: It is sunny, but a bit windy.
The rain is heavy this afternoon.
I have not been outside yet today.
sections.heading: How to answer when someone asks about the weather
steps: Notice the wind, the rain or the sun.
Say what you are wearing or doing.
Say it honestly if you do not know.

sections.body:
Talking about the weather is useful because it changes what you wear.

When it is hot, wear a hat and light clothes. Drink water often. Say no to playing in the sun for too long. The middle of the day is the strongest sun.

When it is cold, wear layers. A shirt, then a jumper, then a jacket. You can take a layer off when you get warm. That is why layers work.

When it rains, take a coat with a hood, not an umbrella if the wind is strong. Wet feet make you cold later, even on a warm day.

When it is windy, hold on to your hat. Keep away from trees and from building edges.

When the sky is dark and grey, the weather can turn fast in the tropics. Keep a small raincoat in your schoolbag, in every month of the year.

And here is the local rule of thumb. In northern Vietnam, the cold season is wet and windy. In the south, the same month is warm and sunny. Ask the people around you what the weather is usually like. They know best.
examples: It is hot, so I am wearing a hat.
It is cold, so I am wearing three layers.
It started to rain, so I put on my coat.
sections.heading: Dressing for the weather

sections.body:
Some weather is not fun to talk about. It is dangerous, and then you need to stay inside.

Thunder and lightning. When you hear thunder, go indoors. Do not stand under a tree. Do not hold a metal thing. Wait until the last thunder has passed before you go out.

A storm with strong wind. Stay away from windows. Move away from trees and from loose things that can fly.

Heavy rain and flooding. Never walk in moving water. It looks shallow and it is not. Go to a higher place and tell an adult.

Very hot sun. Stay inside at midday. Drink water. If you feel dizzy or your head hurts, tell an adult straight away.

Snow and ice. Ice is slippery. Walk slowly. Do not throw snowballs at anybody's head.

When the weather is dangerous, the best thing a child can do is get an adult quickly.
examples: I hear thunder, so I am going inside.
It is very hot, I am staying in at noon.
The wind is strong. Come inside, please.
sections.heading: When the weather is dangerous

item.summary: The weather is the easiest subject in the world to talk about, because everybody has one. After reading this you can describe the sky, tell how hot or cold it is, say what the weather is like, and choose the right clothes for the day.
item.title: Talking About the Weather
